summary: Camden County tower site on a Georgia tower list (8 ft, 'topo 1959' note); no source found on its build, status or access.

events.note: The tnlandforms list gives the note 'topo 1959'. Towers 73 and up were discovered on 1:100,000 USGS topo maps, and this tower is number 390, so the note most likely dates the map on which it was found, not construction.

evidence.supports: White Oak entry: Camden County, elevation 8 ft, note topo 1959, coordinates 31.032222, -81.733611
Names for towers 73 and above are the list's own creation
evidence.quote: (For towers 73 and above, names are my creation.)

evidence.supports: The list's header says towers 1-72 come from the USGS name database and the rest were discovered; tower 390 is in the rest
evidence.quote: Map shows GA fire towers listed by USGS name database (1-72) and as discovered

evidence.supports: The rest were discovered on 1:100,000 USGS topo maps and NGS data sheets, so 'topo 1959' most likely dates the map
evidence.quote: on 1:100,000 USGS topo maps and NGS

evidence.supports: White Oak is an unincorporated community in Camden County
evidence.quote: White Oak is an unincorporated community in Camden County

evidence.supports: The community is located along the coastal highway corridor
evidence.quote: It is located along the coastal highway corridor

notes_for_editor: Single-source record for the tower: the tnlandforms list gives coordinates, elevation and a 1959 topo note, with no build date, design, height, agency, status or access. The name 'white oak' is the list author's own, not a USGS or official name. The Camden County community of the same name is cited for context only; no source ties the tower to it. Wikipedia is used as a lead, not for the tower. Story body is about 125 words. Not verified on the ground.
